title: His father's four-piece string combination
summary: His father played guitar in a four-piece group with De Fuentes, Jim Dorsey and Manetta's uncle; De Fuentes became his first violin teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: I see. Speaking of your grandfather, did he play music?

My father played. My father? Yeah, he played something he was living. In those days, he used to use four pieces, you know, a bass, violin, a guitar, and a violin, and a trumpet, and play a whole ball, you know. They didn't have no big bands like we have today, you know. He was a guitar player. He was a guitar player.
And do you remember any of the fellows he played with?
Well, yeah, they all did. No, there's the violinist. He was my first teacher. His name was De Fuentes. And the bass violin player was Jim Dorsey. And the trumpet player was Mineta. My Mineta's uncle.
Norman, yeah, yes. That's right. That was the four piece combination.
And your teacher, his full name, do you remember?
